concept.body: Regular = all sides equal and all angles equal, so totals divide evenly. Each interior angle = (n − 2) × 180 ÷ n; each exterior = 360 ÷ n; the pair at any vertex sums to 180°. To find n from an interior angle: take 180 minus it (the exterior), then divide 360 by that.

explanationVariants: 360 ÷ 5 = 72° per turn in a regular pentagon.
Five equal turns share the 360° lap: 72° each.

widget.prompt: Each exterior angle of a regular pentagon?

commonErrors.feedback: 108° is each INTERIOR angle. The exterior is its supplement — or directly 360/5 = 72°.
36 = 180 ÷ 5 splits a straight line — the lap is the thing shared: 360 ÷ 5 = 72°.

steps.body: A **regular** polygon is doubly fair: all sides equal AND all angles equal. Fairness makes each angle computable exactly — divide the totals evenly. Each interior angle: **(n − 2) × 180 ÷ n**. Each exterior angle: **360 ÷ n**. Two formulas, one polygon, joined by interior + exterior = 180°.

widget.prompt: Each interior angle of a regular octagon, in degrees?

commonErrors.feedback: 1080 is the TOTAL interior sum — the octagon shares it eight ways: 1080 ÷ 8 = 135°.
45° is each EXTERIOR angle (360/8). Its interior partner is the supplement: 180 − 45 = 135°.

explanationVariants: 360 ÷ 12 = 30° — twelve equal turns share the lap.
The lap splits evenly: 30° per vertex.

widget.prompt: Each exterior angle of a regular 12-gon?

commonErrors.feedback: 150° is each INTERIOR angle. The exterior is its straight-line partner: 180 − 150 = 30° — or directly 360/12.
15 = 180 ÷ 12 splits a straight line — the turns split the full LAP: 360 ÷ 12 = 30°.

steps.body: Going backwards, the exterior route is the shortcut. Told each interior angle is 150°? Don't wrestle (n − 2) × 180/n = 150 — flip to the exterior: 180 − 150 = 30°, then **n = 360/30 = 12**. Supplement first, lap second. Two divisions, done.

explanationVariants: Supplement first (30°), lap second (360/30): a regular 12-gon.

widget.prompt: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 150°. How many sides?

commonErrors.feedback: 5 = 150 ÷ 30 divides interior by exterior — a ratio with no meaning here. Count TURNS in the lap: 360/30 = 12.
6 = 180 ÷ 30 counts turns in a straight line — the lap is 360°: n = 360/30 = 12.

widget.prompt: As a regular polygon gains more and more sides, what happens to each interior angle?

options.label: It climbs toward 180° without reaching it — the shape rounds toward a circle
options.feedback: Each exterior angle 360/n shrinks toward 0, so its interior partner 180 − 360/n creeps up on 180°.

options.label: It shrinks toward 0°
options.feedback: That's the EXTERIOR angle's fate (360/n → 0). The interior does the opposite, rising toward 180°.

options.label: It stays fixed at 108°
options.feedback: 108° belongs to the pentagon alone — each n has its own angle, and they march upward toward 180°.

options.label: It passes 180° for very large n
options.feedback: At 180° the “corner” flattens into a straight line — a convex polygon can approach but never cross it.

widget.prompt: Each interior angle of a regular hexagon? (You can fan it — or supplement 360/6.)

commonErrors.feedback: 720 is the hexagon's TOTAL interior sum — split it six ways: 120°.

hints: Tiles meeting at a point must fill 360° exactly, with no gap and no overlap.
explanationVariants: 360 ÷ 120 = 3 hexagons meet at each point — the honeycomb pattern.
Three corners of 120° fill the full 360° around a point exactly.

widget.prompt: Regular hexagons tile a floor. How many hexagons meet at each point?

commonErrors.feedback: 6 counts the hexagon's SIDES — the question counts corners around a point: 360 ÷ 120 = 3.
4 is the answer for SQUARES (360/90). Hexagon corners are 120°: 360/120 = 3.

takeaways: Regular n-gon: each interior = (n − 2) × 180/n; each exterior = 360/n.
Reversing from an interior angle: supplement first, then n = 360/exterior.
Tilings work when corner angles divide 360° — triangles, squares, hexagons.
